reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Worker A, same AI, separately identified source-first pass. Reconsidered the adopted Appendix 1e and current programme table, inspected the actual specialisation-specific course contents and entry rules again, then compared the exact finished UCR selections, substantive contributions and placements against the current workbook and read all audience selections through the established mapping. This is analytical separation by the same AI, not an independent person or live rendering.
findings: Appendix 1e Articles 37–45 confirms the exact target-named Business Law specialisation within the Dutch full-time Law LLB. It is distinct from CP228’s generic Law route. Thirty compulsory components total sixty credits per year and 180 uniquely; the third year has eight six-credit components, four-credit tax and eight-credit thesis. There is no open minor block to fill. Article 42’s legacy thesis-code suffix is resolved by Article 44, the explicit eight-credit catalogue entry and the programme table.

The moot court requires ninety credits at registration; December results cannot be counted back. Its mandatory activities include court visit, legal documents, pleading training and oral presentation. Thesis teaching requires ninety credits, begins in autumn and runs across the full academic year; normal spring entry is excluded. Completing the first two years satisfies these conditions. The non-credit Dutch test and Talent/Career Development remain requirements; no general-Law Skills Lab rule is imported into the specialisation. Earlier legal introductions precede their specialised continuations.

Read the actual specialisation contents before endorsing correspondence: company law concerns legal forms, lifecycle, corporate groups, reorganisation, investor/creditor protection and takeovers. Law/economics uses incentives, property, transaction costs and liability. Organisation/strategy uses economic organisational theory and competitive advantage; finance integrates accounting, valuation, shareholder litigation and entrepreneurial finance. Ethics combines normative theories with corporate groups, stakeholders, sustainability, rights and litigation. Taxation concerns legal treatment of enterprise, not economic policy alone.

All forty-seven exact-target interests remain reconciled: fourteen eligible generators are covered by the core or two coherent candidates; support and search roles remain bounded. Corporate responsibility/environmental liability substantiate the second priority. The innovative-company candidate is covered by the closest option’s business/finance/AI-governance and legal study but does not produce a genuinely distinct third curriculum. The stopping rule remains two rather than a default of three.

The closest programme materially combines substantial legal study with financial, economic, organisational and strategic analysis; the second retains that legal foundation and accounting while prioritising climate, environmental governance, justice, communication and public-policy analysis. Product prototyping and generic market research are replaced by corporate/economic governance; geology, farming and an unspecified partner project are replaced by economics/accounting, and public policy strengthens regulatory analysis. Every replacement supports the prior concept; none fabricates missing company-law doctrine. The pair differs by sixty credits each way and has a clear sustained substantive difference.

Every selected course contribution was reconsidered from its actual profile or description. Corrected inherited references to other universities’ course names and false direct-equivalence claims. Transnational transactions are not Dutch company formation; rhetoric is not legal procedure; economic taxation is not tax-law doctrine. Public Policy Analysis is given full description-supported consideration. Both schedules meet all actual formal prerequisites, offered terms, twenty-four unique courses, four per term, first-year PPD and six advanced courses; four original offering conflicts are repaired without restoring old values.

Thirteen positive relationships use actual important legal subjects or disciplinary methods and bound differences in scope. Private Law is placed with the broad introduction, Criminal Law with substantive liability, Transnational Business Law with simulated legal-dispute practice, and negotiation only with the ADR part of civil procedure. Accounting/finance directly supports valuation; organisation and ethics are partial relationships. Seventeen dedicated components retain meaningful gaps, including company formation and its advanced doctrine, tax, dedicated procedures and the required thesis. Optional independent research remains outside scheduled credits.

Read the exact finished English title, thirty labels, five selected notes, two concepts, thirteen relationships, seventeen gaps and thirty-two selected descriptions. Audience references, source links and established fallbacks resolve correctly. Unchanged shared descriptions are reused at exact code/name/text versions while case-specific contributions are reassessed. All academic, mechanical and content checks pass; no app/renderer, workbook or enrichment changes, local Shiny/browser launches, screenshots or release approval are claimed.
